Lesson 0 · Beginner · 15 min

Getting started: install Python and run your first script

Install Python on Windows or Mac, open the command line, and run a script, with fixes for the usual first errors.

installing PythonCommand PromptTerminalpip

In this lesson

  • Install Python 3 the right way on Windows or Mac
  • Open Command Prompt or Terminal and move into a folder
  • Run a Python script and read what it prints
  • Install extra libraries with pip
  • Fix the errors that almost everyone meets on day one

Every lesson in this series is a small Python script that you run on your own computer. This lesson sets that up once. It takes about fifteen minutes, and you only do it once.

1. Install Python

  1. Go to python.org, open Downloads, and download the latest Python 3 for your computer.
  2. Windows: run the installer and, on the very first screen, tick the box "Add python.exe to PATH". Then click Install Now. That one box saves most of the trouble later.
  3. Mac: open the downloaded .pkg file and follow the steps.

2. Open the command line

Python scripts are usually run by typing a short command. On Windows, press the Windows key, type cmd and open Command Prompt. On a Mac, press Cmd + Space, type Terminal and press Enter. Check that Python is there by typing the command below and pressing Enter. It should answer with a version number such as Python 3.13.

3. Make a folder and save the script

Make a folder for the lessons, for example python-lessons in your Documents. Open Notepad (Windows) or TextEdit (Mac, then choose Format, Make Plain Text), paste the code below, and save it in that folder as hello.py. You can also click Download on the code box. A code editor such as Visual Studio Code, which is free, makes this easier and colours the code like this page does.

When something goes wrong

'python' is not recognized On Windows, use py instead of python. If py is not found either, run the installer again, choose Modify, and make sure Add Python to environment variables is ticked.

No such file or directory Command Prompt is looking in a different folder. Use cd to move into the folder where you saved the file, and type dir (Windows) or ls (Mac) to see the files there.

SyntaxError Something in the code was typed differently, often a missing quote, bracket or colon. Python shows the line number; compare that line with the lesson.

IndentationError Python uses the spaces at the start of a line to group code. Lines inside a for or with block must be indented by the same amount, usually four spaces.

ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas' The library is not installed yet. Run the pip command above.

Note: Copying the code from this page with the Copy button is the safest way to start. Once a script runs, change one thing at a time and run it again to see what happens.
